lines.japanese: ──よし、分かった。合わせてみるか。
lines.english: —All right. I had her measure. Time to see if I could match her.

lines.japanese: 「なに。なにそれ。なんなのジンクピリチオン」
lines.english: “What? What's that? What even *is* zinc pyrithione?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、あれはですねー、たしかフケ・かゆみをぴしゃりと抑えるんですよ」
lines.english: “Oh, that. I believe it stops dandruff and itching dead.”

lines.japanese: 「なんかー、低薬量で高い抗菌性を示すらしいんですけどー、環境ホルモン作用の可能性も示唆されてましてー」
lines.english: “Apparently it displays powerful antibacterial activity at low concentrations, but there are also indications that it may have endocrine-disrupting effects.”

lines.japanese: はー……そう。そーゆー系か。薀蓄系。いい武器もってんじゃねーか。
lines.english: Ahh... right. So that was her game. A walking encyclopedia. Not a bad weapon to have.

lines.japanese: つーても、そんなムダ知識を偉そうにブン回すだけの語りたがりだったら俺とは合わない。ちょっと試してみよう。
lines.english: Still, if she merely enjoyed brandishing useless knowledge and listening to herself talk, we wouldn't get along. Time for a little test.

lines.japanese: 「いや、そーじゃなくてさ。ソレどんな形してんのジンクピリチオン」
lines.english: “No, that's not what I mean. What shape is zinc pyrithione?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、どうなんでしょうねー。私もまだ見たことないんでー」
lines.english: “Oh, I wonder. I haven't seen one yet myself.”

lines.japanese: ほう。
lines.english: Well.

lines.japanese: 「マジかよ。世の中にはまだまだ不思議がいっぱいだな」
lines.english: “Seriously? The world is still full of mysteries.”

lines.japanese: 「はいー、ホントそうですよねー」
lines.english: “Yes. It really is, isn't it?”

lines.japanese: ほうほう、しっかり落としてきたか。はっ。
lines.english: Well, well. She had stuck the landing. Hah.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあさ。そしたらおまえ、アレ知ってる？　アレ、スパゲティのアレ。ほら、なんだっけ、デュラムセ・モリナ？」
lines.english: “Then do you know that spaghetti thing? You know—the, uh, durum se-molina?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、デュラム・セモリナですかー。やー、あれはですねー、たしか煮崩れしないコシのあるパスタが出来るんですよー」
lines.english: “Oh, durum semolina? Apparently it produces firm pasta that won't fall apart when boiled.”

lines.japanese: 「マジで？　そしたらアルデンテとかお手のもんじゃん。すげーなデュラムセ・モリナ。何者なの」
lines.english: “Seriously? Then al dente must be child's play. Durum se-molina is amazing. What sort of creature is it?”

lines.japanese: 「えーとー、なんかデュラム小麦をセモリナした粉のことらしいんですけどー、パスタ法の定められてるイタリアだと、乾燥パスタは１００％純正のデュラム・セモリナを使わないと怒られちゃうぐらいでー」
lines.english: “Let's see. Apparently it's flour made by semolina-ing durum wheat, and in Italy, where pasta has its own laws, they get angry if dried pasta isn't made from one hundred percent pure durum semolina.”

lines.japanese: 「いや、そーじゃなくて。どんな形してんのデュラムセ・モリナ」
lines.english: “No, that's not what I mean. What shape is durum se-molina?”

lines.japanese: 「あー、どうなんでしょうねー。私もまだ見たことないんでー」
lines.english: “Oh, I wonder. I haven't seen one yet myself.”

lines.japanese: 「マジかよ。世の中にはまだまだ不思議がいっぱいだな」
lines.english: “Seriously? The world is still full of mysteries.”

lines.japanese: 「はいー、ホントそうですよねー」
lines.english: “Yes. It really is, isn't it?”

lines.japanese: 小娘がにっこり笑う。台詞は白々しくても、表情は素なんじゃないかと思った。
lines.english: The girl smiled. Her line was patently insincere, but I thought the expression itself might be real.

lines.japanese: ぎらついた夜の繁華街。やたらと語尾を引っぱられた間抜けな言葉たちが、クレープ屋を包むバニラの香りのあいだをふわふわと漂っているみたいだ。
lines.english: The entertainment district glittered in the night. Those foolish words, their endings drawn out far too long, seemed to float weightlessly through the vanilla fragrance surrounding the crêpe shop.

lines.japanese: ヘンなやつ。
lines.english: Weird girl.

lines.japanese: と思った。だって、俺がおもしれえと思うやつは決まってヘンなやつだ。
lines.english: So I thought. Everyone I found interesting was invariably strange.

lines.japanese: ここで余談──
lines.english: A brief digression—

lines.japanese: たとえばシューズショップで靴を探しているとしよう。とりあえず足を入れてみる。残念ながらサイズが合わないかもしれないし、そうでなくても新しい靴は慣れるまで痛みを引きずることが珍しくない。
lines.english: Suppose you're looking for shoes in a shoe store. First you try a pair on. They may be the wrong size; and even if they aren't, new shoes often hurt until you break them in.

lines.japanese: 最初からぴったりフィットする靴に出会う確率ってのは、もしかしたらそう高くはないのかもな。
lines.english: Perhaps the odds of finding a shoe that fits perfectly from the start aren't especially high.

lines.japanese: ──だからなんだって話。
lines.english: —And your point is?

lines.japanese: 「ねーちゃん、あんたなかなか話せる子だねぇ」
lines.english: “Miss, you can really hold a conversation.”

lines.japanese: 「いえいえー、とんでもないですー」
lines.english: “Oh, no, no. Nothing of the kind.”

lines.japanese: 小娘は頭を前に倒して、その先でてのひらを左右に振った。パルさんはいつの間にかバンの中に戻って、鉄板から甘い匂いを漂わせていた。
lines.english: The girl bowed her head and waved one hand rapidly in front of it. At some point Paru had returned inside the van, where a sweet aroma now rose from the griddle.

lines.japanese: 「あとさ、おまえさアレ知ってるアレ、栄養ドリンクのほら、タウリン？」
lines.english: “Hey, do you know that thing from energy drinks? Taurine?”

lines.japanese: 「ドラ、もういいよ。コマーシャルで耳にはするものの意味よく分かんない単語特集はもういいから」
lines.english: “Dora, that's enough. No more words everybody's heard in commercials and nobody actually understands.”

lines.japanese: クレープ屋はクレープ板でクレープを焼きながら言う。
lines.english: The crêpe seller said this while cooking a crêpe on the crêpe griddle.

lines.japanese: 「冗談は置いといてさ。ドラ、この子の自転車探し、引きうけてやっとくれよ」
lines.english: “Joking aside, Dora, take the job. Find this girl's bicycle for her.”

lines.japanese: 俺は後ろ頭をがしがし掻きながら眉間に皺を刻んだ。
lines.english: I scratched furiously at the back of my head and carved a crease between my brows.

lines.japanese: 「いや、じゃあ俺も冗談抜きで返答させてもらうけど……スンマセン無理です」
lines.english: “Then let me answer without joking either... I'm sorry. Can't be done.”

lines.japanese: 「はいー、ですよねー」
lines.english: “Yes. Of course it can't.”

lines.japanese: 俺がきっぱり断言すると、早すぎるくらい早い笑顔が返ってきた。
lines.english: My refusal was categorical; her smile returned almost too quickly.

lines.japanese: いや、そんな泣きそうな顔されても。
lines.english: Come on. Don't make a face like you're about to cry.

lines.japanese: 「だってホント悪りぃけどさ、ただ漠然とチャリ探せってそんな、どう考えたって無理じゃん。タランチュラを掴むような話だって」
lines.english: “I really am sorry, but telling me to find one vague, unspecified bike—it's obviously impossible. You might as well ask me to grab a tarantula.”

lines.japanese: 「あ？　クモを掴むようなって、そっちの蜘蛛だったか？」
lines.english: “Huh? Grasping at a spider? Isn't it supposed to be grasping at straws?”

lines.japanese: 「えー、まー、雲違いなんですけどー、発言者の意図は伝わりましたので」
lines.english: “Well, wrong sort of thing to grasp, but we understood the speaker's intent.”

lines.japanese: 「そうそれ。悪いけどタランチュラ」
lines.english: “Yeah, that. Sorry, but this one's a tarantula.”

lines.japanese: 張りのない声で下に向けて言いながら、俺はそそくさと車体の陰にフェイドアウトした。
lines.english: I aimed the lifeless words at the ground and hurriedly faded from sight behind the van.

lines.japanese: 残念ながら商談決裂。中断していた清掃作業を再開しよう。
lines.english: Regrettably, negotiations had broken down. Time to resume the cleaning I had interrupted.

lines.japanese: 「は～あ、参ったねどうも。甲斐性のない男もいたもんだよ」
lines.english: “Haaah. What a disappointment. I never knew a man could be so useless.”

lines.japanese: 「やー、いえそんな、普通の反応だと思いますよ普通のー」
lines.english: “Oh, no. I think his reaction was perfectly normal. Perfectly normal.”

lines.japanese: 車体の向こうで、女たちが誰かの噂をしている。
lines.english: On the other side of the van, the women were gossiping about somebody.

lines.japanese: 関係ないやと思った。
lines.english: Nothing to do with me, I decided.
